claims.claim: Hermas, the author of The Shepherd of Hermas, was a former slave who was emancipated and became a Roman businessman.
Hermas was born in Aquileia, Italy, in the Roman Empire.
The Muratorian fragment identifies Hermas as the brother of Pope Pius I, who was bishop of Rome around 140-155 CE.
The most likely date for The Shepherd of Hermas's origin is approximately 140 CE.
The Shepherd of Hermas is a Christian literary work of the late first half of the second century.
The work was composed in Greek.

The Shepherd of Hermas was written to address the moral decline of the contemporary church and to direct readers and hearers to repentance and the resuscitation of the virtues of the primitive church.
The author recommends a second absolution of sins to be granted after baptismal absolution, authorized by a letter from heaven.
The work consists of five visions, twelve mandates or commandments, and ten similitudes (parables).
The Shepherd of Hermas was popular among Christians in the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th centuries.
